# 具身操作算法实习生. 1.研发机器人操作算法,重点突破灵巧手抓取、精细装配、多物体操作等任务,提升机器人在复杂场景下的操作能力; 2.开发基于学习的操作策略(模仿学习、强化学习等),实现动态环境下的自适应抓取与操作; 3.探索端到端操作框架,结合大语言模型(LLM)与视觉-动作映射,实现“感知→决策→执行”的高效闭环; 4.基于仿真平台(如Isaac Sim、MuJoCo)构建高保真操作训练环境,加速算法迭代与真实机器人部署; 5.参与前沿操作算法研究(如触觉反馈利用、非刚性物体操作、多模态操作策略等)。. 1.硕士或博士在读,机器人学、人工智能、计算机等相关领域; 2.操作算法经验: 熟悉机器人抓取、装配等操作任务,有灵巧手或双臂协同项目经验者优先; 了解力控(如阻抗控制)、触觉反馈或非刚性物体操作技术; 3.学习与优化: 掌握模仿学习、强化学习等算法,有操作策略训练经验(如GraspNet、Diffusion Policy等); 熟练使用PyTorch/TensorFlow,具备机器人仿真(Sim2Real)经验者加分; 4.工程能力: 熟练使用Python/C++,熟悉ROS/ROS2基础框架; 具备扎实的代码调试与算法部署能力。 加分项 1.在机器人操作领域(如抓取、装配、触觉操作等)发表过顶会论文(ICRA、IROS、CoRL等); 2.有机械臂操作相关经验或项目 实习收获 1.聚焦机器人操作核心技术,参与场景落地项目; 2.接触真实人形机器人和灵巧手操作; 3.开放的研究氛围,支持成果发表与专利申报。. 牛客安全提示:如发现虚假招聘、广告,或以任何名义索要证件、费用,或诱导异地入职、参与培训等均属违法行为,发现请 立即举报. 0 笔试题目 0 面试经验 0 面试短评.

公司自建全国所有和海外近70个国家渠道。在智能建造领域,大规模应用于中国建筑、中国电建、浙建集团等央国企。在智慧工地实名制领域,全国市占率超70%,市占率第一。在智慧社区领域,是移动、联想、电信三大运营商的主要产品供应商,在数万小区展开落地应用。在智慧园区/楼宇领域,构建人、车、资产、安防、能源等一体化管理系统,在当虹科技总部大楼、河南龙湖金融中心等标志性场景落地解决方案。

| 我们正在建设面向具身智能的仿真训练与真实场景执行系统。该岗位的最终目标不是只在仿真中获得较高成功率,而是让机器人进入真实的商店、客厅、厨房等场景,安全、稳定地完成导航、抓取、放置、整理和人与机器人协作等任务。该岗位负责打通从仿真场景、任务与数据构建,到策略训练、真机集成、现场调试和真实任务评测的完整链路。候选人需要具备良好的机器人系统与 Python 工程能力,能够定位感知、规划、控制、通信、硬件和环境之间的系统性问题,并对机器人在真实场景中的最终执行结果负责。## 工作职责- 在 RoboCasa、MuJoCo、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill、robosuite 或其他平台中搭建机器人仿真场景。- 将 3D 资产转换并配置为 USD、URDF、MJCF 等仿真格式,完成尺度、坐标系、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节和物理属性设置。- 根据真实商店、客厅、厨房等目标环境构建数字化场景,配置机器人、相机、光照、传感器和可操作物体,并控制仿真与实景之间的关键差异。- 设计具身智能任务,明确 instruction、initial state、action space、success condition、failure condition、reset distribution 和 benchmark split。- 为模仿学习、强化学习、Diffusion Policy、ACT、VLA 和 LeRobot 等训练流程生成、清洗和管理轨迹数据。- 将仿真或数据训练得到的策略部署到真实机器人,完成模型转换、推理服务、机器人接口、传感器接入和控制链路集成。- 在真实场景中完成机器人标定、定位、导航、抓取与操作调试,包括相机内外参、手眼标定、坐标系、末端执行器和动作精度校准。- 设计并实施 sim-to-real 方案,包括域随机化、系统辨识、真实数据回采、策略微调和仿真参数校准。- 组织真实机器人任务测试,建立现场部署、任务初始化、失败恢复、人工接管、日志回传和重复实验流程。- 分析真机失败案例,区分感知、规划、控制、通信、策略、硬件和场景因素,并推动问题闭环。- 为真实环境中的人员、设备和物体制定安全约束,落实速度与力限制、碰撞保护、急停、工作空间限制和异常降级机制。- 开发自动化场景与任务检查工具,检测穿模、碰撞体错误、动力学异常、不可达、不可抓取、任务无法重置和成功判定失效等问题。- 建立贯通仿真与真机的可复现训练和评测 pipeline,对比成功率、碰撞率、恢复率、任务耗时、泛化能力和 sim-to-real gap。- 设计场景、物体、初始状态和语言指令的随机化方案,并控制训练集、验证集和测试集之间的泛化难度。- 使用 Codex 等 Agent 工具辅助代码开发、批量实验、数据清洗、结果分析和失败案例归因。- 与生成式 AI Agent 与 3D 资产工程师协作定义资产接入标准,与世界模型研究工程师协作定义交互数据和策略接口。- 参与机器人学习、sim-to-real、真实场景部署和 benchmark 方向的创新研究与论文工作。##
requirements: - 熟悉 Python,能够独立完成仿真环境、数据处理、实验脚本和自动化工具开发。- 理解机器人学基础,包括坐标变换、位姿、运动学、轨迹、碰撞检测、传感器和控制等概念。- 具有真实机器人开发或实验经验,能够进行设备连接、标定、动作调试、日志分析和故障排查。- 熟悉 Linux 环境,能够使用 ROS 或 ROS 2 完成机器人、传感器和算法模块之间的集成。- 了解机器人操作、导航、模仿学习或强化学习中的至少一个方向,并理解从模型输出到真实机器人动作执行的完整链路。- 理解 mesh、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节、材质、相机和尺度等仿真资产概念。- 能够定义清晰、可执行、可自动评测的机器人任务,并将同一任务协议落实到仿真和真实环境。- 具备较强的问题拆解、现场调试和工程执行能力,愿意参与真实场景搭建、真机实验和迭代部署。## 加分项- 熟悉 MuJoCo、RoboCasa、robosuite、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill 或 Habitat 中的一个或多个平台。- 熟悉 imitation learning、reinforcement learning、Diffus

articles.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
articles.summary: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. articles.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
articles.summary: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. articles.summary: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. articles.summary: Current humanoid dexterous manipulation remains largely confined to end-effectors and simple grasps, falling short of humans' ability to engage the entire body by bracing and sliding bulky objects against the arms and torso. articles.summary: The effective deployment of humanoid robots in practical tasks of interest will require a capability of sensing and adapting to variations in inertial parameters, as occurs during heavy tool use or when carrying significant payload. articles.summary: Embodied Visual Tracking (EVT) is an essential capability for intelligent robots in human-robot collaboration, requiring an agent to follow a designated target person in dynamic environments relying solely on egocentric visual perception. articles.summary: Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. articles.summary: Many vision-language-action policies rely on action-labeled robot demonstrations and lack an explicit mechanism for predicting future visual states. articles.summary: Continuous physical human-robot interaction requires robots to rapidly adapt their control behaviour without interrupting task execution. articles.summary: Reliable contact-rich manipulation requires detecting execution deviations early enough for corrective action. articles.summary: Online decision-making faces a tension between efficient inference and long-horizon reasoning. Value-based methods rely on short-horizon bootstrapping that limits the propagation of long-term information, while trajectory optimization methods plan explicitly but must solve a high-dimensional optimization problem at every decision step. We propose Generative Trajectory Planning (GTP), a model-based framework that addresses this tension by learning a generative model as a proposal distribution over action sequences. articles.title: Known-Voice Cloning and the Limits of Personality Transfer for Character Design
articles.summary: Recent advances in zero-shot voice cloning systems make it possible to reproduce a recognizable voice from a short recording and attach it to arbitrary virtual characters. Prior work suggests that familiar vocal identity can carry over associated personality impressions to new targets such as robots or virtual characters. However, these works have mainly examined familiarity and personalization effects rather than directly testing whether a cloned familiar voice systematically transfers personality impressions to an embodied virtual character. Such transference raises the concern that cloned voices could be used to manipulate people into engaging with virtual characters as capable social actors. Across two studies, we investigated whether personality impressions transfer when a virtual character speaks with the cloned voice of a familiar person. Study 1 examined this question in a real-world university setting using the cloned voice of a lecturer familiar to the participating students.

articles.title: ForkCast: Predictive Recovery for Vision-Language-Action Policies via Counterfactual Futures
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies perform manipulation tasks using camera images and language instructions, but object slip or visual occlusion can disrupt execution. Recovery is typically learned during policy training or delegated to a monitor that triggers a scripted repair after detecting a failure. We introduce ForkCast, a predictive recovery framework that compares counterfactual futures to determine whether and how to intervene in a frozen VLA policy. At each decision point, ForkCast evaluates three candidates: executing the policy's nominal action chunk (Commit), adjusting the camera viewpoint (Reobserve), and replanning the arm trajectory (Replan). articles.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models
articles.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. Existing continual RL methods on top of VLAs mitigate forgetting but rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, whereas off-policy methods improve single-task sample efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. articles.title: WAVE-0: Bridging VLA Policies and WAMs with Lightweight Latent Future Prediction
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies excel at generalist robotic manipulation but generate actions without explicitly modeling their environmental consequences. World action models (WAMs) incorporate future prediction, yet most rely on costly video generation, while latent alternatives either use predicted futures only as auxiliary targets or infer latent actions from suboptimal visual transitions through costly large-scale video pretraining. We introduce WAVE-0 (World-model-Augmented VLA Execution), a framework that bridges VLAs and WAMs through a lightweight latent world model. By connecting the semantic understanding of pretrained VLAs with explicit future prediction, WAVE-0 allows anticipated action consequences to directly guide action generation. articles.title: MemoryVLN: From Ego-Aware Memory Representation to Cross-Context Memory Reuse in Vision-Language Navigation
articles.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have shown strong potential for embodied vision-language navigation (VLN), yet their performance degrades on long-horizon trajectories due to context-length limits, redundant historical observations, and unstable spatial alignment across time. These issues make it difficult to both compress long navigation histories and reliably reuse past spatial experience. articles.title: Thinker-WM: A Unified World Model with Shared Multimodal Representations for Embodied Intelligence
articles.summary: World models have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied AI, yet existing systems often remain fragmented in the modalities they model and the functions they support. In particular, visual dynamics, geometric structure, and executable action are commonly coupled through separate interfaces or downstream modules rather than being jointly represented and evolved within a shared dynamics model. articles.title: PACT: Posture-Aligned Co-Design Technique for Hand Configuration and Retargeting in Multi-Finger Imitation Learning
articles.summary: The fidelity of teleoperated demonstrations used for imitation learning is determined by how faithfully a robot hand can replicate the operator's posture. The posture retargeting law that the robot will execute is typically selected only once the hardware has been finalized, and conventional hand designs often neglect human-like grasping postures.
